Pale red; 10R-6/2 and light greenish gray 5GY-8/1; silty calcareous mudstone with limestone

Sandstone: moderate brown (5YR 3/4) to dark yellowish-brown (10YR 4/4); silt to very fine-grained; angular; fairly well sorted; quartz; mudstone matrix; fairly firm; interbedded with mudstone and limestone near base.

Mudstone and Limestone: Mudstone; grayish-red (5R 4/2) with very dusky red-purple (5RP 2/2) bands; partly silty; and calcareous. Limestone; grayish-red (5R 4/2) to pale red (5R 6/2) and light red (5R 6/8); aphanitic to very finely crystalline; and shaly. Little sandstone near top.

Claystone; Siltstone; and Limestone: Claystone; grayish-red (5R 4/2) with very dusky red-purple (5RP 2/2) bands; partly silty; calcareous in upper portion; gradational with mudstone above. Siltstone; very pale reddish-brown (10R 6/4) to grayish-orange-pink (5YR 7/2); argillaceous cement; fairly firm; with lenses of moderate dark yellowish-brown (10YR 4/4) clayey siltstone. Limestone; grayish-red (5R 4/2) to pale red (5R 6/2) and light red (5R 6/6); aphanitic to very finely crystalline; and shaly.

Claystone: grayish-red (5R 4/2) near base; gradational upward to medium red (5R 4/4) to medium reddish-brown (10R 4/4); with light greenish-gray (5G 8/1) spots and limestone pellets throughout; slightly silty; slightly calcareous; grades to siltstone at top.

Siltstone; Claystone; and Sandstone: Siltstone; medium reddish-brown (10R 4/4) to moderate red (5R 4/6) and grayish-red (10R 4/2); mostly with argillaceous cement; fairly firm; siltstone predominent in upper part of unit; grades upward from claystone. Claystone; medium reddish-brown (10R 4/4) to moderate red (5R 4/6); and moderate to dark yellowish-brown (10YR 5/4-4/4); becomes silty towards middle of unit; absent at top. Sandstone; white (N 9) to medium gray (N 5) and moderate red (5R 5/4); speckled; silt to fine-grained; angular to sub-angular; poorly sorted; quartz and arkose with claystone particles; arenaceous to argillaceous cement; fairly firm; slightly calcareous; sandstone less than 5% of lower half of unit; absent near top.

Claystone and Sandstone: Claystone; medium reddish-brown (10R 4/4) to moderate red (5R 4/6); and grayish-red (10R 4/2); moderate to dark yellowish-brown (10YR 5/4-4/4) in upper half of unit; silty with quartz and arkose grains. Sandstone; white (N 9) to medium gray (N 5) and moderate red (5R 5/4); speckled; silt to fine-grained; angular to sub-angular; poorly sorted; quartz and arkose with claystone particles; arenaceous to argillaceous cement; fairly firm; slightly calcareous. Unit may be correlative with Perea sandstone member of Chinle formation.

Claystone: medium reddish-brown (10R 4/4) to moderate red (5R 4/6) and grayish-red (10R 4/2); with few spots of light greenish-gray (5GY 8/1); light grayish-red-purple (5RP 5/2) near top of unit (appears clastic); slightly silty; slightly calcareous; and few limestone pellets; mostly near base of unit.

Claystone; Limestone; and Sandstone: Claystone; dusky red (5R 3/4) to moderate to dark reddish-brown (10R 4/6-3/4) with light greenish-gray (5G 8/1) spots; partly waxy; partly silty to sandy (mudstone); partly slightly calcareous; and with limestone pellets. Limestone (pellet form); medium light to medium dark gray (N 6-4) to dark grayish-red (5R 4/2); aphanitic to very finely crystalline; and partly shaly. Sandstone; dusky red (5R 3/4) to dark reddish-brown (10R 3/4) and light greenish-gray (5G 8/1 - 5GY 8/1); very fine- to fine-grained; sub-angular to sub-rounded; fairly well sorted; quartz and clastic mudstone; argillaceous and calcareous cement; fairly firm; sandstone with coarse-grained rounded; clear to milky quartz particles near middle of unit. Conglomerate bed 50 feet below top of unit; vari-colored; fine- to coarse-grained; sub-rounded to rounded; poorly sorted; quartz; mudstone; and limestone particles; argillaceous cement; fairly firm; some mudstone particles up to granule-size; conglomerate grades from sandstone.

Sandstone: very light gray (N 8); grayish-red (5R 4/2); and moderate reddish-brown (10R 4/6); speckled; very fine- to fine-grained; partly medium-grained; sub-angular to sub-rounded; fairly well sorted; quartz; argillaceous and calcareous cement; fairly firm; claystone flakes abundant in some beds. Mudstone and claystone beds near base.

Mudstone and Claystone: Mudstone; dark reddish-brown (10R 3/4) to grayish-red (5R 4/2) and medium light gray (N 6); silty to sandy; grades to sandstone in upper 100 feet of unit; and calcareous. Claystone; reddish-brown (10R 4/4) to dusky red (5R 3/4) and grayish-red-purple (5RP 4/2); with light grayish-green (5G 8/1) spots; partly silty; partly calcareous; and with limestone pellets. Limestone (pellet form); moderate olive-brown (5Y 4/4); pale yellowish-brown (10YR 6/2) to medium light to medium dark gray (N 6-4); and dark grayish-red (5R 4/2); aphanitic to very finely crystalline; partly shaly.

Sandstone: white to very light gray (N 9-8); fine- to medium-grained; with few granules; sub-angular to rounded; fairly well sorted; quartz; arenaceous to argillaceous (red) cement; firm. Mudstone and claystone minor in upper part of unit.

Mudstone; Claystone; Limestone; and Sandstone: Mudstone; grayish-red (5R 4/2) to dark reddish-brown (10R 3/4) and greenish-gray to light greenish-gray (5G 6/1-8/1); with little light olive brown (5Y 5/6); silty with mica flakes; and calcareous. Claystone; medium gray (N 5) and dusky red (5R 3/4) to dark reddish-brown (10R 3/4); light to moderate greenish-gray (5G 8/1-7/1); and grayish-purple (5P 5/2); partly waxy; partly mottled red and green. Limestone; (pellet form); very pale yellowish-brown (10YR 7/2) to very pale purple (5P 7/2) to grayish-purple (5P 4/2) to moderate yellowish-brown (10YR 5/4) to medium dark gray (N 4); aphanitic to very finely crystalline. Sandstone; white to very light gray (N 9-8) near base of unit; pale red (10R 6/2) to pale reddish-brown (10R 5/4) to very light gray (N 8) in middle and upper parts; very fine- to fine-grained; sub-angular to sub-rounded; fairly well sorted; quartz; argillaceous to arenaceous cement; firm.

Mudstone and Claystone: blackish-red (5R 2/2) to dusky red (5R 3/4) to moderate reddish-brown (10R 4/6) to dusky purple (5P 2/2) with inter bands of medium to dark gray (N 5-3) to greenish-gray (5G 6/1) to dark greenish-gray (5GY 4/1); mudstone beds silty to sandy; partly calcareous; claystone beds waxy. Limestone (pellet form); of two types: (1) grayish-black (N-2) to grayish-red (5R 4/2); aphanitic to very finely crystalline; and shaly; pellets with dark center and red near edge; predominent near base of unit; and (2) very pale yellowish-brown (10YR 7/2) and very pale purple (5P 7/2); aphanitic to very finely crystalline; predominant in middle and upper parts. Coal in lowermost 20 feet of unit.

Sandstone and Mudstone: Sandstone; white to very light gray (N 9-8); very fine- to fine-grained; angular to sub-angular; fairly well sorted; clear quartz; arenaceous cement; fairly firm; mica flakes along bedding planes. Mudstone; medium to medium dark gray (N 5-4) to greenish-gray (5G 6/1); partly dark reddish-brown (10R 3/4) to blackish-red (5R 2/2); silty to sandy; partly calcareous; mudstone mostly at top of unit.

Mudstone and Sandstone: Mudstone; dark reddish-brown (10R 3/4) to very dusky red (10R 2/2) to blackish-red (5R 2/2) predominent near base of unit; and medium to medium dark gray (N 5-4) to greenish-gray (5G 6/1); partly dark grayish-purple (5P 3/2); predominent near top; silty and sandy; slightly calcareous near top of unit. Sandstone; white (N-9); very fine- to fine-grained; angular to sub-angular; fairly well sorted; clear quartz; arenaceous cement; fairly firm; sandstone predominent in lower 20 feet of unit.
